docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The Ultimate RAG

A powerful Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that generates cited responses from your local documents.

Get Started Try it Live

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Ultimate RAG is a powerful Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed to provide accurate, source-cited answers to your questions. Simply upload your documents (.pdf, .docx, .txt), and the application will build a local knowledge base. You can then query this knowledge base in natural language, and the system will generate a response, citing the specific sources from your documents.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Format Support

    Upload documents in .txt, .docx, .pdf, and more. The system builds a local knowledge base for you to query.

  • Secure & Private

    Features robust user authentication and stores all your data locally using PostgreSQL and Qdrant.

  • Powered by Gemini

    Leverages Google's Gemini API for state-of-the-art response generation, with support for other models.

  • Easy to Deploy

    Comes fully containerized with Docker, allowing for a quick and isolated setup.

docs.title: Start Your Journey
docs.text:
• 1. Install

    Follow our straightforward installation guide to get The Ultimate RAG running locally. Go to Installation

  • 2. Try the Demo

    Learn how to use the application, from uploading documents to crafting the perfect query. Read the User Guide

docs.text:
The deployment architecture of The Ultimate RAG is designed to ensure reliable, scalable, and isolated environments for testing and production.

graph TD
    subgraph Test Environment
        TEST_SPACE[Hugging Face Space <br> Test Server] -->|Connects to| TEST_DB[Test PostgreSQL Database]
        TEST_SPACE -->|Runs| APP_TEST[Docker Container: Application]
    end

    subgraph Production Environment
        PROD_SPACE[Hugging Face Space <br> Production Server] -->|Connects to| PROD_DB[Production PostgreSQL Database]
        PROD_SPACE -->|Runs| APP_PROD[Docker Container: Application]
    end

    subgraph CI/CD Pipeline
        GITHUB[GitHub Repository] -->|Push to| TEST_SPACE
        TEST_SPACE -->|Integration Tests Pass| PROD_SPACE
    end

    subgraph External Services
        TEST_DB -->|Hosted on| DB_SERVICE[Supabase]
        PROD_DB -->|Hosted on| DB_SERVICE
    end

    classDef server fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000;
    classDef db fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000;
    classDef pipeline fill:#bfb,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000;
    class TEST_SPACE,PROD_SPACE,APP_TEST,APP_PROD server;
    class TEST_DB,PROD_DB db;
    class GITHUB pipeline;
  • Diagram Location: The deployment diagram is stored at docs/architecture/deployment-view/deployment.mmd.

Deployment Choices:

  • Hugging Face Spaces: We use Hugging Face Spaces for both test and production environments due to their ease of use, free tier, and seamless integration with Git-based deployment. This allows rapid deployment and automatic scaling for our Python application.
  • Docker: The application is containerized using Docker (defined in docker-compose.yml) to ensure consistency across test and production environments, simplifying dependency management and deployment.
  • Separate PostgreSQL Service: The test and production PostgreSQL databases are hosted on an external service (not Hugging Face) to provide scalability, isolation, and robust database management. This ensures that test data does not interfere with production data.
  • Isolation of Environments: Separate Hugging Face Spaces and databases for test and production prevent test activities from affecting the live application, ensuring stability for end users.

Customer Deployment: Customers can access the application directly via the production Hugging Face Space at [URL to be provided]. No local deployment is required, as the application is hosted and managed on Hugging Face. To interact with the application, customers need:

  • A web browser to access the production URL.
  • Optional: API keys or credentials (contact the DevOps lead for access details, if applicable). If customers prefer to deploy the application locally, they can follow the Installation instructions in this README, which include cloning the repository, setting up Docker, and configuring a .env file with a PostgreSQL connection string (contact the DevOps lead for details).

docs.title: Continuous Deployment
docs.text:
Our Continuous Deployment (CD) pipeline automatically deploys the application after a successful merge into the main branch. This ensures that new features and fixes are quickly delivered to users following thorough testing.

The pipeline is managed using GitHub Actions and is defined in:

  • .github/workflows/sync-to-hf.yml

docs.title: CD Pipeline Steps
docs.text:
The CD pipeline follows a sequential, controlled process to ensure stable deployments:

  1. Pushes the updated code to a Hugging Face Space (test environment) using git, where it is automatically deployed.
  2. Runs integration tests on the test server with a test PostgreSQL database (hosted on a separate service), using tests located in app/tests/integration.
  3. If integration tests pass, deploys to a separate Hugging Face Space (production environment) with a production PostgreSQL database (also hosted on a separate service). Deployment takes approximately 2–3 minutes.
  4. If any tests fail, the production server remains unaffected.

docs.title: Deployment Tools:
docs.text:
• Docker: Builds and packages the application as a container.
  • git: Pushes the application to Hugging Face Spaces for deployment.

docs.title: Testing Tools:
docs.text:
• pytest: Runs integration tests on the test server.

All CD workflow runs can be viewed at:

  • GitHub Actions - CD Workflow Runs

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
Our Continuous Integration (CI) pipeline ensures code quality by running automated checks on every pull request to the main branch. This critical process helps maintain a robust and secure codebase.

The pipeline is managed using GitHub Actions and is defined in:

  • .github/workflows/unit-tests.yml

docs.title: Static Analysis Tools:
docs.text:
These tools help identify potential errors, enforce coding standards, and scan for security vulnerabilities without running the code.

  • flake8: A linter for Python that enforces coding style and detects common programming errors.
  • bandit: A security vulnerability scanner for Python, designed to identify potential security issues in the codebase.

docs.title: Testing Tools:
docs.text:
These tools are used to execute automated tests that verify the functionality of the code.

  • pytest: A comprehensive testing framework for Python, used to run unit tests located in app/tests/unit.

If any CI checks fail, the pull request cannot be merged into main. All CI workflow runs can be viewed and reviewed at:

  • GitHub Actions - CI Workflow Runs

These automated checks are essential for maintaining the integrity and quality of our codebase.

docs.title: Git workflow
docs.text:
We have developed our custom workflow due to CI/CD integration issues and features of the development process.

Key Principles

  • main is always deployable.
  • Feature branches are created from main and merged back via Pull Requests (PRs).
  • No long-lived branches except for_testing, which serves for deploy to the testing server.

docs.title: 1. Issues
docs.text:
• Use the one of the Issue Templates.
  • Include: Description, Labels, and Milestone.
  • Assign the most logically suitable label from the list of labels (read their description first).
  • Assign the issue to yourself, and contact PM to re-assign if needed.

docs.title: 2. Branching
docs.text:
• For developing new feature create a new branch.
  • There are now strict rules for naming, but each name should logically depict the changes on code (e.g. add response streaming → response_stream).
  • For each merge mention the reason why branches were merged.

docs.title: 3. Commit Messages
docs.text:
• Template: <type>(<scope>): <description>.
  • Examples:
Text Only
feat(auth): add login button
fix(api): resolve null pointer in user endpoint

docs.title: 4. Pull Requests (PRs) and Reviews
docs.text:
• Use the PR Template.
  • Target branch - main, but for testing for_testing can be used.
  • Contact PM to assign Reviewers.
  • Merge pull request if the code passes review, tests and linter (in other case you will be unable to do it).
  • Delete branch after merge.

docs.title: 5. Resolving Issues
docs.text:
• Close manually only after:
    • PR is merged.
    • Feature is verified in production (if applicable).

docs.title: Secrets management
docs.text:
Security First: Never Commit Secrets

To maintain the security of our application, sensitive information like API keys and database credentials are not stored in the repository. Access is managed by the DevOps lead.

docs.title: Requesting Secrets
docs.text:
To get the necessary secrets for your local .env file, please follow these steps:

  1. Contact the DevOps Lead: Reach out to @Andrchest via GitHub.
  2. Provide Context: Briefly explain the issue or feature you are working on that requires access to the secrets.
  3. Receive Securely: The DevOps lead will provide you with the content for your .env file through a secure channel.

This process ensures that our production keys remain safe and access is logged.

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Bash
git clone https://github.com/The-Ultimate-RAG/The-Ultimate-RAG.git
cd The-Ultimate-RAG

docs.title: Configure Environment Variables
docs.text:
Copy the Template

Create a file named .env in the root directory. Copy the contents of the block below into it and fill in your details.

Critical: Do Not Commit Your .env File

Your .env file contains sensitive secrets like your API key. It should never be pushed to GitHub. The repository's .gitignore file is already configured to prevent this, but you should always be careful.

.env
# --- Database link ---
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:mysecretpassword@localhost:5432/rag_db

# --- Large Language Model API Key ---
# 🔑 Get your key from Google AI Studio. You can swap this for Mistral if you don't have any.
GEMINI_API_KEY=your-gemini-api-key

# --- Security Settings ---
# 🔐 A random string used for an extra layer of password security.
SECRET_PEPPER=your-super-secret-pepper-string
JWT_ALGORITHM=HS256

docs.title: Set Up a Python Virtual Environment
docs.text:
It's highly recommended to use a virtual environment to manage project dependencies.

On macOS/Linux:On Windows: Bash
python3 -m venv env
source env/bin/activate
Bash
python -m venv env
.\env\Scripts\activate

docs.title: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
Bash
pip install -r ./app/requirements.txt

docs.title: Launch the Application
docs.text:
Ensure Docker is Running

Before proceeding, make sure your Docker daemon is active.

docs.title: Run Qdrant Vector Database
docs.text:
Important: Use an Absolute Path for Data Persistence

The -v flag in the Docker command ensures your vector database data persists across container restarts.

Replace $(pwd)/database or %cd%/database with the absolute path to a directory on your host machine where you want Qdrant to store its data.

On macOS/Linux:On Windows (Command Prompt): Start Qdrant
docker run -p 6333:6333 -p 6334:6334 -v "$(pwd)/database:/qdrant/storage: qdrant/qdrant
Start Qdrant
docker run -p 6333:6333 -p 6334:6334 -v "%cd%/database:/qdrant/storage" qdrant/qdrant

docs.title: Wait for Qdrant Initialization
docs.text: Allow a moment for the Qdrant container to fully start and initialize before proceeding to the next step. You can check its logs with docker logs <container-id-or-name>.

docs.title: Run the Main Application
docs.text:
Once Qdrant is ready, launch the core application from your activated virtual environment. Launch Application

python -m app.core.main

docs.title: Access the Server
docs.text:
Once the containers are up and running, open your web browser and navigate to: http://127.0.0.1:5050

You should see the application's welcome page. To stop the application, press Ctrl+C in the terminal where the script is running.

docs.title: Time behavior
docs.text:
Importance to Customer

The customer wants the system to work fast, as slow response times would negatively impact user experience and productivity. For a RAG system, quick retrieval and generation are critical for usability.

Scenario Stimulus Source Artifact Environment Response Response Measure Test Execution System response time for queries User submits a query through the web interface without files End user Response generation pipeline Normal operation System returns answer with citations within 10 seconds 95% of queries should complete within 10 seconds - Use request generating tools (httpx, postman api) for multiple concurrent user simulation- Measure time from query submission to full response display- Test with various query lengths and complexities Document ingestion processing time User uploads a new document End user Document processing pipeline Normal operation Document is processed and available for queries within 50 seconds 90% of documents under 5MB should process within 50 seconds - Upload sample documents of various sizes and types- Measure time from upload request receiving to the appearance of a document in corresponding folder- Validate the content of the saved document by comparing with the sample one

docs.title: Functional completeness
docs.text:
Importance to Customer: The customer requires comprehensive documents format support (.pdf, .txt, .doc, .docx, .json, .csv) and the ability to directly examine citation sources. This ensures users can work with their existing documents and verify information accuracy through proper source examination.

Scenario Stimulus Source Artifact Environment Response Response Measure Test Execution Supported documents extensions User uploads a document End user Document processing pipeline Normal operation System accepts and properly processes the document 100% success rate for supported extensions (.pdf, .txt, .doc, .json, .csv, .docx) - Upload test documents of various extensions from the defined list- Validate the content of the saved document by comparing with the sample one Citation source examination User clicks on a citation in the response End user Document viewer system Normal operation System opens the source document at the exact citation location 100% of citations should link to correct document location - For each supported file type: - Upload sample document - Generate queries that produce citations - Click each citation link - Verify: - Correct document opens - View is focused on cited section - Highlighting/indication of exact citation location is visible (not supported for pdfs)

docs.title: Functional correctness
docs.text:
Importance to Customer: The customer wants the system to cite only relevant information. Accurate citations are crucial for the system's credibility and usefulness in research or decision-making scenarios (especially, for EAP-2).

Scenario Stimulus Source Artifact Environment Response Response Measure Test Execution Citation relevance User submits a query End user Retrieval component Normal operation All provided citations directly support the generated response At least 90% of citations should be judged relevant by domain experts - Prepare a set of test queries with known correct answers or integrate LLM- Generate response for each test query and validate (use LLM or domain-experts)- Calculate percentage of relevant citations Answer accuracy User submits a factual query End user LLM component Normal operation Generated answer matches known correct information 95% of factual queries should return correct answers - Use a validation set of questions with verified answers- Compare system output to ground truth (via LLM)- Calculate accuracy percentage

docs.title: 1. Registration test
docs.text: Description: Check if a new user can successfully sign up to save the history of his chats. How to test: The new user should access the registration page (/new_user) manually or via pressing button "+ Add new chat" and enter (valid) credentials. Acceptance criteria: GIVEN an unauthenticated user on the registration page WHEN the user enters a valid email (proper format) and password (at least on latter in uppercase, at least one special symbol, at least one digit, at least 8 characters in length), confirms the password (enters the same password) THEN registration is successful, the user is redirected to the main (chat) page, and able to communicate.

docs.title: 2. Response seed test
docs.text: Description: Check if a authorized user can receive an answer to the query with attached document(s) within a minute. How to test: Authorize the user (register a new one, or log in with an existing one), enter any query (at least written in human understandable manner) and attach relevant documents (content of the file should be logically suitable for the query), wait a response. Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the authorized user on the chat page WHEN the user attaches file (file extension should be in the list .pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt, .json, .csv, .md, file content should suit the query) and asks a question (in any language, but language of attached files is preferred) THEN the user gets a valid response (comprehensive answer for the initial query with at least one cited file from the attached ones in the language of initial query) within a minute.

docs.title: 3. Multiple chat creation test
docs.text: Description: Check if the authorized user is able to create multiple chats in one section and the message history is saved. How to test: Authorize the user (register a new one, or log in with an existing one), enter any query (at least written in human understandable manner) and attach relevant documents (content of the file should be logically suitable for the query), wait a response. Click on the button "+ Add new chat". Repeat first instruction. Return to the previous chat. Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the authorized user on the chat page WHEN the user attaches any file and enters any query, or just enters any query, waits the response, repeats this ones more time in a new chat, and returns back to the any old chat THEN the user is able to see previously asked questions and system responses with clickable and valid citations (after a click the document can be seen by the user).

docs.title: 4. Response streaming test
docs.text: Description: Check if the authorized user is able to receive an answer from the system chunk by chunk and do not have to wait until the full response is ready. How to test: Authorize the user (register a new one, or log in with an existing one), enter any query (at least written in human understandable manner) and attach relevant documents (content of the file should be logically suitable for the query), hit the "ask" button, and check if the response is sent part by part. Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the authorized user on the chat page WHEN the user attaches file (file extension should be in the list .pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt, .json, .csv, .md, file content should suit the query) and asks a question (in any language, but language of attached files is preferred) THEN the user can see how a valid response (comprehensive answer for the initial query with at least one cited file from the attached ones in the language of initial query) is being received part by part (user can already see its parts and start to read the response).

docs.title: 5. Response language test
docs.text: Description: Check if the authorized user is able to receive an answer from the system in the language, defined by the query. Additionally, checks if the system is able to cite documents written in different languages. How to test: Authorize the user (register a new one, or log in with an existing one), enter any query (in any language, but language of attached files is preferred) and attach relevant documents (content of the file should be logically suitable for the query, can be written in any language), hit the "ask" button, and wait for the response. Acceptance criteria: GIVEN the authorized user on the chat page WHEN the user attaches file (file extension should be in the list .pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt, .json, .csv, .md, file content should suit the query), written in any language and asks a question (in any language, but language of attached files is preferred) THEN the user can see the generated valid response (comprehensive answer for the initial query with at least one cited file from the attached ones) in the language, defined by the initial query, and click on cited documents, after that the user should be redirected to the document viewer with loaded document in the language, defined by the initial file, and see the cited place.

docs.title: Error: Port is already allocated
docs.text:
This means another service on your machine is using port 5050, 6333, or 6334.

Solution: Stop the conflicting application or change the ports in your docker run command and .env file.

docs.title: Application can't connect to Qdrant
docs.text:
This usually happens if you run python -m app.core.main before the Qdrant Docker container has fully initialized.

Solution: Stop the Python app (Ctrl+C), wait about 30 seconds for the database to start, and then run the app again. You can check Docker logs to see when Qdrant is ready.

docs.title: Error: SECRET_PEPPER is not set
docs.text:
The application will not run without all environment variables being configured.

Solution: Ensure you have created the .env file in the root directory and copied all the required fields from the template in the installation guide.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text: You can try the currently deployed version of the system here. Follow these steps to get started:

docs.title: Access the Site
docs.text: You should see the main page with the system's name.

docs.title: Start a New Chat
docs.text: Press the + Add new chat button and wait for the login page to load.

docs.title: Navigate to Registration
docs.text: Find and click the Register button.

docs.title: Sign Up
docs.text:
On the sign up page, enter your credentials.

For Testing

You can use Test1@test1.com in all fields for quick testing.

docs.title: Submit and Wait
docs.text:
Click ONLY ONCE on the Sign Up button.

Patience is Key

The initial chat page may take around 10 seconds to load after signing up. Please wait.

docs.title: Start Chatting!
docs.text: You can now ask questions and attach files. Type your query in the input area and press Enter.
